A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PEARL and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. The material supports reliable comparison despite pagination and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original PEARL experiments, including accuracy comparisons, ablations, forgetting measurements, and resource-allocation analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original PEARL experimental results and analyses, alongside an expanded baseline comparison in Appendix Table 10.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 newly states that thresholds T>1 are clipped to 1, whereas v1 asserts that T cannot exceed 1. The core algorithm is retained, but the PDFs do not establish whether clipping changes the implementation or documents an existing safeguard.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-R coverage, Class-IL and Task-IL scenarios, and ImageNet pretraining data. The additional Table 10 baselines introduce no new dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Appendix Table 10 adds CLS-ER, IMEX-Reg, and SARL to the existing Seq-CIFAR100 (5T) and Seq-TinyImageNet (10T) comparisons. Previously included comparators remain.

E3.justification: Dataset partitions, backbones, evaluation metrics, and PEARL training settings remain unchanged. Table 10 retains its Class-IL/Task-IL protocol and rehearsal-buffer size of 200.

E4.justification: The rank, target-module, reinitialization, learning-rate, class-order, pretraining, forgetting, and resource-allocation analyses are retained. Table 10 adds standard benchmark comparisons rather than a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same three-run and standard-deviation reporting, randomized class-order analysis, and resource-allocation comparisons across runs. The added Table 10 rows follow the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 10 adds results for three baselines while retaining existing scores. SARL reports TinyImageNet Task-IL accuracy of 71.56±0.18, above the unchanged PEARL R18 and BSC means of 71.49±0.23 and 70.94±0.44. This changes the reported ranking without establishing a statistically significant difference.

T1.justification: v3 removes Proposition 3.2 and its incorrect proof that T≤1, acknowledging that T can reach 2. Equation 4 replaces T_mu with T and removes the scalar-mean explanation. The SVD formulation and Theorem 3.1 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: rehearsal-free continual learning through dynamic LoRA rank allocation across three architectures. Broad claims of outperforming all considered baselines are also retained.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 newly explains that Equation 4's existing +1 term prevents zero-rank projections and preserves minimal expressive capacity. Broader result interpretations and Appendix A.4's limitations concerning model growth, task boundaries, and full-model fine-tuning remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents clipping T>1 to 1 in the implementation. Appendix C's architecture, optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, and epoch details remain unchanged; no new code or data access information is provided.

R1.justification: Five cited works are added, including those underlying CLS-ER, IMEX-Reg, and SARL, plus two earlier continual-learning works cited in the introduction. Existing research positioning remains largely unchanged. A duplicate TriRE reference is removed while the work remains cited.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the threshold discussion, the explanation of +1, citation updates, and an author-affiliation correction. The overall narrative and main-text/appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 10 expands to include three additional rows and revised ranking emphasis. Table 4 moves from page 9 to page 8, with accompanying text reflow. All five figures retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: Removing the false threshold bound and documenting clipping improve mathematical accuracy and reproducibility, while Table 10 provides stronger comparison coverage. The gain is limited: existing PEARL results are unchanged, and Section B.6 still claims universal outperformance despite SARL's higher reported TinyImageNet Task-IL mean.
